a425.t:
Na sede do partido, em São Vicente, o parlamentar fala da falta investimento para aumentar a injecção de renováveis na rede.
“Desde logo, é preciso que a empresa de distribuição de combustível utilize os combustíveis mais baratos. Nós temos Porto Novo e Fogo, que deveriam utilizar fuel 180 e infelizmente não estão a utilizar por razões de logística. A UCID pede ao governo para rapidamente executar os leilões que permitam que haja mais energia renovável no país e que esta energia seja injectada na rede para que o consumidor final, quer as famílias, quer as empresas, possam ter acesso a custos de energia muito mais aceitável do que aquilo que é neste momento”, defende.
António Monteiro defende que o país deve aproveitar todos os mecanismos disponíveis para investir e reduzir o preço da electricidade. O deputado sugere o recurso às verbas do Fundo Climático e Ambiental e do terceiro Compacto do Millennium Challenge Corporation.
“A questão que se coloca é que nós temos que aproveitar todas as oportunidades que o país possa dispor. Mas, infelizmente, o que nós temos é que, desde 2010-2011, estamos em 2024, há 13 anos que não temos um investimento de relevo na questão de melhoria de energias renováveis em Cabo Verde. Isto é inadmissível e daí termos os custos de energia das mais elevadas do mundo neste momento”, afirma.
O partido recorda que ter energia mais cara impacta negativamente a vida dos cabo-verdianos e retira competitividade às empresas.
“O aumento da energia em Cabo Verde tem um impacto altamente negativo no bolso dos contribuintes e acaba por retirar a competitividade das empresas cabo-verdianas, do país e impacta negativamente na vida do dia-a-dia dos cidadãos. E este aumento da electricidade vem fazer com que, ao invés de continuarmos a ter a inflação a baixar, com este aumento, a tendência do aumento da inflação aumenta consideravelmente”, refere.
A UCID defende o combate às perdas que, entre Janeiro a Setembro do ano passado, representaram 1/4 da energia produzida pela Electra, a nível nacional. O partido considera que é preciso evitar que parte dessa perda seja introduzida na tarifa cobrada aos consumidores.
De acordo com as tabelas em vigor desde 1 de Janeiro, na ELECTRA, as tarifas de electricidade sofreram um aumento de 2,12 ECV/kWh em todos os escalões. Na AEB, as novas tarifas aumentaram 3,57 ECV/kWh.
a425.en:
At the party headquarters in São Vicente, the member of parliament speaks of the lack of investment to increase the injection of renewables into the grid.

"First of all, the fuel distribution company must use cheaper fuels. We have Porto Novo and Fogo, which ought to be using fuel 180 and unfortunately are not using it for logistical reasons. UCID asks the government to carry out quickly the auctions that would allow more renewable energy in the country and for this energy to be injected into the grid so that the final consumer, both families and companies, can have access to much more acceptable energy costs than those at present," he argues.

António Monteiro argues that the country should take advantage of all available mechanisms in order to invest and reduce the price of electricity. The deputy suggests resorting to the funds of the Climate and Environment Fund and of the third Millennium Challenge Corporation Compact.

"The question that arises is that we have to take advantage of all the opportunities the country may have available. But, unfortunately, what we have is that, since 2010-2011, and we are in 2024, for 13 years we have had no significant investment in the matter of improving renewable energy in Cape Verde. This is unacceptable, and hence we have some of the highest energy costs in the world at this moment," he states.

The party recalls that having more expensive energy negatively impacts the lives of Cape Verdeans and takes away competitiveness from companies.

"The increase in energy in Cape Verde has a highly negative impact on taxpayers' pockets and ends up removing the competitiveness of Cape Verdean companies and of the country, and negatively impacts citizens' day-to-day lives. And this electricity increase means that, instead of continuing to have inflation falling, with this increase the trend of rising inflation increases considerably," he notes.

UCID advocates combating the losses which, between January and September of last year, represented 1/4 of the energy produced by Electra nationally. The party considers that it is necessary to prevent part of that loss from being introduced into the tariff charged to consumers.

According to the tables in force since 1 January, at ELECTRA electricity tariffs underwent an increase of 2.12 ECV/kWh in all brackets. At AEB, the new tariffs increased by 3.57 ECV/kWh.

a443.t:
(Une alliance éducative renforcée)
Depuis quelques années, l’École Internationale de Graphisme (EIG Bénin) et l’Institut de Formation et de Recherche en Informatique (IFRI-UAC) bâtissent ensemble un pont solide entre l’éducation et les métiers du numérique et du design. Cette collaboration fructueuse a permis de concevoir et de mettre en place des formations innovantes, alignées sur les exigences du marché du travail et les attentes des étudiants. Aujourd’hui, nous sommes fiers d’annoncer le renouvellement de notre partenariat, marquant une nouvelle phase de croissance et d’opportunités pour nos étudiants. Ce renforcement de notre collaboration s’inscrit dans une dynamique de développement académique et professionnel, avec des perspectives encore plus ambitieuses.
Les axes stratégiques du partenariat
Ce partenariat stratégique avec l’IFRI nous permet d’explorer de nouvelles opportunités et de consolider notre engagement commun en faveur de l’excellence académique. À travers cette coopération, nous nous engageons à : Renforcer nos programmes de formation afin d’offrir aux étudiants de l’IFRI et de l’EIG des cursus enrichis et adaptés aux exigences du marché. Développer des projets et des solutions innovantes dans les domaines de l’informatique, de l’électronique et du numérique, favorisant ainsi la mise en pratique des compétences acquises en cours. Co-créer des formations certifiantes et co-signées par les deux institutions, permettant aux étudiants et aux professionnels d’accéder à des certifications reconnues sur le marché du travail. Proposer des formations en design et graphisme aux étudiants de l’IFRI, leur permettant ainsi d’acquérir des compétences complémentaires essentielles dans le monde du digital. Offrir des stages d’immersion au sein des studios de l’EIG, afin de permettre aux étudiants de l’IFRI d’intégrer des environnements professionnels et de développer leur employabilité.
Un engagement mutuel pour l’excellence académique
Le renouvellement de ce partenariat témoigne de la confiance et de la vision partagée entre nos institutions. Nous remercions chaleureusement le Professeur Eugène C. EZIN, Directeur de l’IFRI-UAC, pour son engagement et son soutien constant à cette collaboration. Professeur titulaire des universités CAMES, Membre de l’IEEE Computer Science Society, Auteur de plus d’une trentaine de publications scientifiques dans des revues internationales, son expertise et son implication dans la recherche et l’innovation renforcent la pertinence et la valeur de ce partenariat.
Une collaboration tournée vers l’avenir
En renouvelant notre engagement avec l’IFRI, nous affirmons notre volonté de contribuer activement à l’évolution de l’éducation et de la formation en Afrique. Nous sommes convaincus que cette collaboration permettra d’ouvrir encore plus de portes aux étudiants, en leur offrant des opportunités académiques et professionnelles à la hauteur de leurs ambitions. EIG, Créons l’Afrique Créative.
a443.en:
Renewal of the Partnership between IFRI (UAC) and EIG Benin: A strategic collaboration in the service of academic excellence
(A strengthened educational alliance)
For some years now, the International School of Graphic Design (EIG Benin) and the Institute of Training and Research in Computer Science (IFRI-UAC) have together been building a solid bridge between education and the digital and design professions. This fruitful collaboration has made it possible to design and put in place innovative training programmes, aligned with the requirements of the labour market and the expectations of students. Today, we are proud to announce the renewal of our partnership, marking a new phase of growth and opportunities for our students. This strengthening of our collaboration is part of a dynamic of academic and professional development, with even more ambitious prospects.
The strategic pillars of the partnership
This strategic partnership with IFRI allows us to explore new opportunities and to consolidate our shared commitment to academic excellence. Through this cooperation, we undertake to: Strengthen our training programmes in order to offer IFRI and EIG students enriched curricula adapted to market requirements. Develop innovative projects and solutions in the fields of computing, electronics and digital technology, thereby promoting the practical application of skills acquired in class. Co-create certifying courses co-signed by the two institutions, enabling students and professionals to access certifications recognised on the labour market. Offer training in design and graphic arts to IFRI students, thereby allowing them to acquire essential complementary skills in the digital world. Offer immersion internships within EIG's studios, in order to enable IFRI students to enter professional environments and develop their employability.
A mutual commitment to academic excellence
The renewal of this partnership bears witness to the trust and shared vision between our institutions. We warmly thank Professor Eugene C. EZIN, Director of IFRI-UAC, for his commitment and constant support for this collaboration. A full professor of the CAMES universities, a member of the IEEE Computer Science Society, author of more than thirty scientific publications in international journals, his expertise and his involvement in research and innovation strengthen the relevance and value of this partnership.
A collaboration turned towards the future
In renewing our commitment with IFRI, we affirm our desire to contribute actively to the evolution of education and training in Africa. We are convinced that this collaboration will make it possible to open even more doors for students, by offering them academic and professional opportunities equal to their ambitions. EIG, Let's Create Creative Africa.

Muktasari:
- Tunaweza kusema hatua hii muhimu ni mwisho au mwanzo za zamani nyingine ndani Konde Music ila haiondoi ukweli kwamba hadi hapa tulipofika, kuna eneo Harmonize hana deni kwa wasanii wote waliopita katika lebo hiyo
Dar es Salaam. Hatimaye rekodi lebo ya Konde Music Worldwide yake Harmonize imeridhia msanii wake wa pekee na wa kwanza kumsaini, Ibraah kuondoka baada ya kufanya kazi pamoja ya kutoa burudani kwa mashabiki kwa takribani miaka mitano.
Tunaweza kusema hatua hii muhimu ni mwisho au mwanzo za zamani nyingine ndani Konde Music ila haiondoi ukweli kwamba hadi hapa tulipofika, kuna eneo Harmonize hana deni kwa wasanii wote waliopita katika lebo hiyo.
Baada ya sakata la Ibraah kuomba kuondoka katika lebo hiyo kufika mbele ya Baraza la Sanaa Taifa (Basata) ili kupata usuluhishi, Harmonize ameibuka na kusema haina haja ya kufika huko kwa msanii aliyemtoa yeye, hivyo anamtakia kila la heri.
Ikumbukwe Ibraah alitambulishwa Konde Music mnamo Aprili 2020 akiwa ndiye msanii wa kwanza kisha wakafuata wengine watano ambazo ni Country Wizzy, Cheed, Killy, Anjella na Young Skales kutokea Nigeria.
Harmonize alitangaza rasmi kuanzisha lebo ya Konde Music hapo Oktoba 10, 2019 ikiwa ni kipindi kifupi baada ya kujitoa katika lebo ya WCB Wasafi yake Diamond Platnumz ambayo ilimtoa kimuziki kupitia wimbo wake, Aiyola (2015).
Tunasema hana deni kwa sababu wasanii wote saba waliowasaini Konde Music kashirikiana nao na nyimbo walizotoa zimefanya vizuri, na hiki ndicho wanakifuata wasanii wengi katika lebo za wasanii wakubwa wakiamini ushawishi wa bosi wao kimuziki utawasaidia.
Tangu amejiunga Konde Music mwaka 2020, kila mwaka Ibraah alikuwa anatoa wimbo na Harmonize, tayari wameshirikiana katika nyimbo tano ambazo ni One Night Stand (2020), Addiction (2021), Mdomo (2022), Tunapendeza (2023) na Dharua (2024).
Kolabo yao ya kwanza na ya mwisho, ndizo zimefanya vizuri zaidi, hadi sasa video ya wimbo, One Night Stand (2020) imetazamwa YouTube zaidi ya mara milioni 22, huku Dharua (2024) ikitazamwa mara milioni 21 ndani ya mwaka mmoja.
Inaelezwa kuwa Harmonize alimkuta Ibraah amesharekodi wimbo, One Night Stand (2020) akaupenda na kuomba kuongeza vesi yake kitu ambacho Ibraah alikubali na ulipotoka ukafanya vizuri na kumtambulisha zaidi.
Kwa ujumla chini ya Konde Music, Ibraah ametoa EP tatu, Steps (2020), Karata 3 (2021) na Air Piano (2024) pamoja na albamu moja, The King of New School (2022) ambayo haikushirikisha msanii yeyote wa lebo hiyo.
Msanii mwingine aliyebebwa sana na kolabo za Harmonize pale Konde Music ni Anjella, wawili hao wameshirikiana kwenye nyimbo tano ambazo ni All Night (2021), Kama (2021), What Do You Miss (2021), Kioo (2022) na Toroka (2022).
Video ya wimbo, Kioo (2022) imetazamwa zaidi ya mara milioni 9.9 You Tube na ndio video pekee ya Anjella ambayo imepata namba kubwa zaidi katika mtandao huo unaotumika na mashabiki wengi wa muziki nchini.
Na Anjella ndiye msanii pekee wa kike aliyeshirikishwa katika albamu ya pili ya Harmonize, High School (2021), hii ni tofauti na albamu ya kwanza, Afro East (2020) ambayo ilishirikisha wasanii wawili tu wa kike, Lady Jaydee na Yemi Alade.
Kwa upande wake Country Wizzy, kabla ya kujiunga na Konde Music, tayari alishasikika katika wimbo wa Harmonize, Bedroom Remix (2020) ambao ulikutanisha wasanii wengine kama Darassa, Billnass, Nay wa Mitego, Moni Centrozone, Rosa Ree n.k.
Baada ya kusaini Konde Music, Country Wizzy alitokea katika video ya wimbo wa Harmonize, Jeshi (2020), huku naye Harmonize akitokea katika video ya ngoma ya Country Wizzy, Intro (2020) iliyomtambulisha katika lebo hiyo.
Muda mfupi uliofuatia, wawili hao wakatoa wimbo uliofanya vizuri sana, Far (2020) ambao hadi sasa video yake ndio namba moja kwa kutazamwa zaidi YouTube kwa Country Wizzy, rapa aliyefunika na albamu yake, Yule Boy (2019) yenye nyimbo 30.
Ikumbukwe baada ya Country Wizzy kuachana na Konde Music hapo Januari 2022, alienda kuanzisha lebo yake, I Am Music ambayo ilikuja kulisaini kundi la Hip Hop, Fresh Boys lenye wasanii wanne.
Nao Cheed na Killy ambao walijiunga na Konde Music baada ya kujitoa Kings Music yake Alikiba, licha ya kazi zao kuchelewa kutoka, hawakuondoka mikono mitupu katika lebo hiyo kwani kila mmoja alitoa EP na zote Harmonize alishiriki.
Cheed alitoa EP yake, Endless Love (2022) yenye nyimbo sita huku Harmonize akishiriki katika wimbo ‘Konkodi’ ila kwa bahati mbaya hadi Cheed anaondoka Konde Music kufuatia mkataba wake kusitishwa, video ya wimbo huo ilikuwa haijatoka.
Naye Killy alitoa EP, The Green Light (2020) yenye nyimbo sita pia huku Harmonize akisikika katika wimbo ‘Ni Wewe’ ambao video yake imeshatazamwa YouTube zaidi ya mara milioni 21 ikishika namba moja kwa msanii huyo.
Tukija kwa Young Skales wa Nigeria, huyo kabla ya kujiunga na familia ya Konde Music, alishafanya kolabo kadhaa na Harmonize kama Fire Waist (2018), Oyoyo (2019), Oliver Twist II Remix (2020) n.k.
Kwa muktadha huo, Harmonize anaweza kuhukumiwa kwa mambo mengine kama ya kiutendeji ndani ya Konde Music Worldwide lakini linapokuja suala la muziki, hana deni upande huo, alijitoa kikamilifu kwa kila aliyemsaini na sasa amebaki pekee yake.
a476.en:
Summary:
- We can say this important step is the end, or the beginning of another era, within Konde Music, but it does not remove the fact that, up to the point we have reached, in one respect Harmonize owes nothing to all the artists who have passed through that label.

Dar es Salaam. Finally, Harmonize's record label Konde Music Worldwide has agreed to let its unique, first-signed artist, Ibraah, leave, after they worked together entertaining fans for almost five years.

We can say this important step is the end, or the beginning of another era, within Konde Music, but it does not remove the fact that, up to the point we have reached, in one respect Harmonize owes nothing to all the artists who have passed through that label.

After the saga of Ibraah asking to leave the label reached the National Arts Council (Basata) for arbitration, Harmonize came out and said there was no need to go there over an artist whom he himself brought out, and so he wishes him all the best.

It should be recalled that Ibraah was introduced at Konde Music in April 2020 as the label's first artist, and then five others followed, namely Country Wizzy, Cheed, Killy, Anjella and Young Skales from Nigeria.

Harmonize officially announced the founding of the Konde Music label on 10 October 2019, a short while after he pulled out of Diamond Platnumz's WCB Wasafi label, which had launched him musically through his song Aiyola (2015).

We say he owes nothing because he collaborated with all seven artists signed to Konde Music and the songs they released did well, and this is what many artists are looking for at big artists' labels, believing that their boss's musical influence will help them.

Since he joined Konde Music in 2020, every year Ibraah released a song with Harmonize; they have already collaborated on five songs: One Night Stand (2020), Addiction (2021), Mdomo (2022), Tunapendeza (2023) and Dharua (2024).

Their first and their last collaborations are the ones that did best: to date the video of the song One Night Stand (2020) has been viewed on YouTube more than 22 million times, while Dharua (2024) has been viewed 21 million times within one year.

It is said that Harmonize found that Ibraah had already recorded the song One Night Stand (2020), liked it and asked to add his own verse, something Ibraah accepted, and when it came out it did well and gave him greater exposure.

Overall, under Konde Music, Ibraah released three EPs - Steps (2020), Karata 3 (2021) and Air Piano (2024) - together with one album, The King of New School (2022), which did not feature any artist from that label.

Another artist greatly carried by Harmonize's collaborations at Konde Music is Anjella; the two have worked together on five songs: All Night (2021), Kama (2021), What Do You Miss (2021), Kioo (2022) and Toroka (2022).

The video of the song Kioo (2022) has been viewed more than 9.9 million times on YouTube and is the only Anjella video to have achieved the biggest numbers on that platform, which is used by many music fans in the country.

And Anjella is the only female artist featured on Harmonize's second album, High School (2021); this differs from the first album, Afro East (2020), which featured only two female artists, Lady Jaydee and Yemi Alade.

For his part, Country Wizzy, before joining Konde Music, had already been heard on Harmonize's song Bedroom Remix (2020), which brought together other artists such as Darassa, Billnass, Nay wa Mitego, Moni Centrozone, Rosa Ree and others.

After signing with Konde Music, Country Wizzy appeared in the video of Harmonize's song Jeshi (2020), while Harmonize also appeared in the video of Country Wizzy's song Intro (2020), which introduced him at that label.

A short time later, the two released a song that did very well, Far (2020), whose video is to date number one in views on YouTube for Country Wizzy, a rapper who made his mark with his album Yule Boy (2019), containing 30 songs.

It should be recalled that after Country Wizzy parted ways with Konde Music in January 2022, he went on to found his own label, I Am Music, which went on to sign the hip hop group Fresh Boys, which has four artists.

As for Cheed and Killy, who joined Konde Music after leaving Alikiba's Kings Music, although their works were slow in coming out, they did not leave that label empty-handed, because each released an EP and Harmonize took part in all of them.

Cheed released his EP, Endless Love (2022), with six songs, with Harmonize featuring on the song 'Konkodi', but unfortunately, by the time Cheed left Konde Music following the termination of his contract, the video of that song had not been released.

Killy also released an EP, The Green Light (2020), also with six songs, with Harmonize heard on the song 'Ni Wewe', whose video has been viewed on YouTube more than 21 million times, ranking number one for that artist.

Coming to Young Skales of Nigeria, before he joined the Konde Music family he had already done several collaborations with Harmonize, such as Fire Waist (2018), Oyoyo (2019), Oliver Twist II Remix (2020) and others.

In that context, Harmonize can be judged on other matters, such as management within Konde Music Worldwide, but when it comes to the question of music, he owes nothing on that side: he gave himself fully to everyone he signed, and now he has been left on his own.

By: Franklin ASARE-DONKOH
Information coming from the seat of government has it that the Chief of Staff, Mr. Julius Debrah has annulled all appointments and recruitments made into the Public Services after December 7, 2024.
A letter containing the directive has been sent to all heads of government institutions.
According to the Chief of Staff, the appointments did not comply with established good governance practices and principles.
The statement further instructed all heads of government institutions to take immediate steps to nullify such appointments and recruitments and submit a comprehensive report on the actions taken by February 17, 2025.

Muktasari:
- Mwinyi Zahera, aliyewahi kufanya kazi kwa karibu na Ibenge wakati wakiinoa timu ya taifa la DR Congo, ametoa ushauri kwa Wananchi kuelekea mchezo huo ambao utachezwa Jumanne ya Novemba 26 Uwanja wa Benjamini Mkapa, akitoa tahadhari na mbinu za kukabiliana na Al-Hilal.
Kwa sasa Yanga iko katika hatua muhimu kuelekea mchezo wao wa kwanza wa hatua ya makundi ya Ligi ya Mabingwa Afrika dhidi ya mabingwa wa Sudan, Al-Hilal Omdurman. Katika kujiandaa kwa mchezo huo, wamevujishiwa mbinu na rafiki wa karibu wa kocha wa Al-Hilal, Florent Ibenge.
Mwinyi Zahera, aliyewahi kufanya kazi kwa karibu na Ibenge wakati wakiinoa timu ya taifa la DR Congo, ametoa ushauri kwa Wananchi kuelekea mchezo huo ambao utachezwa Jumanne ya Novemba 26 Uwanja wa Benjamini Mkapa, akitoa tahadhari na mbinu za kukabiliana na Al-Hilal.
Zahera, ambaye kwa sasa ni Mkurugenzi wa ufundi wa Namungo amewaambia Yanga kuwa makini sana katika kujenga mashambulizi yao.
Alisisitiza kuwa, kama watashindwa kuwa makini, wanaweza kukutana na mashambulizi ya kushtukiza kutoka kwa Al-Hilal, kama ilivyotokea kwenye mchezo wa mwisho baina ya timu hizo.
“Yanga wanahitaji kuzingatia zaidi katika kujilinda na kutokubali mashambulizi ya haraka ya Al-Hilal. Hawa ni mabingwa wa Sudan, na mara nyingi wanapocheza nje ya uwanja wao wanaweza kuwa hatari sana katika mashambulizi ya kustukiza,” alisema Zahera.
Yanga na Al-Hilal walikutana kwa mara ya mwisho Oktoba 8, 2022, katika mchezo wa raundi ya pili wa kuwania nafasi ya kuingia hatua ya makundi ya Ligi ya Mabingwa. Katika mchezo huo, walitoka sare ya 1-1 jijini Dar es Salaam, lakini Yanga ilitupwa nje baada ya kupoteza ugenini mchezo wa marudiano kwa bao 1-0. Mchezo huo uliwaacha Wananchi na maumivu, lakini pia somo muhimu kuhusu jinsi ya kukabiliana na timu ngumu kama Al-Hilal.
“Ibenge ni mtaalamu wa kutumia mbinu za kushtukiza na kubadilika haraka. Yanga wanahitaji kuwa na nidhamu na kuzingatia katika dakika zote za mchezo. Hii itawasaidia kuepuka mashambulizi ya ghafla ambayo Al-Hilal wanaweza kutumia wakati wowote,” alisisitiza Zahera.
Zahera aliwataka Yanga kucheza kwa nidhamu na kutokubali kupoteza mpira kirahisi katika maeneo ya hatari.
a832.en:
Yanga given the tactics to finish off Al-Hilal

Summary:
- Mwinyi Zahera, who once worked closely with Ibenge when they were coaching the DR Congo national team, has given advice to the Wananchi (Yanga) ahead of the match to be played on Tuesday, 26 November, at the Benjamin Mkapa Stadium, issuing warnings and tactics for dealing with Al-Hilal.

Yanga are currently at an important stage ahead of their first group-stage match in the African Champions League against the Sudanese champions, Al-Hilal Omdurman. In preparing for that match, they have been given leaked tactics by a close friend of Al-Hilal's coach, Florent Ibenge.

Mwinyi Zahera, who once worked closely with Ibenge when they were coaching the DR Congo national team, has given advice to the Wananchi ahead of the match to be played on Tuesday, 26 November, at the Benjamin Mkapa Stadium, issuing warnings and tactics for dealing with Al-Hilal.

Zahera, who is currently the technical director of Namungo, has told Yanga to be very careful in building their attacks.

He stressed that if they fail to be careful, they could face surprise counter-attacks from Al-Hilal, as happened in the last match between the two teams.

"Yanga need to concentrate more on protecting themselves and not allowing Al-Hilal's quick attacks. These are the champions of Sudan, and often when they play away from home they can be very dangerous on surprise attacks," said Zahera.

Yanga and Al-Hilal last met on 8 October 2022, in the second-round match to contest a place in the group stage of the Champions League. In that match they drew 1-1 in Dar es Salaam, but Yanga were knocked out after losing the away return leg 1-0. That match left the Wananchi in pain, but also with an important lesson about how to deal with tough teams like Al-Hilal.

"Ibenge is an expert at using surprise tactics and changing quickly. Yanga need to have discipline and concentration for all the minutes of the match. This will help them avoid the sudden attacks that Al-Hilal can use at any time," Zahera emphasised.

Zahera urged Yanga to play with discipline and not to lose the ball easily in dangerous areas.

a1503.t:
State-owned agricultural land will soon be released for farming - a major milestone in the agrarian reform process, says President Cyril Ramaphosa.
Last week the department of agriculture, land reform and rural development announced that members of the public will be able to apply to lease 700 000 hectares of underutilised or vacant state land in seven of the provinces.
"Agricultural land is the mainstay of our natural resource base. The availability and sustainable use of farmland to grow crops and for animal husbandry is key to our very survival," he said.
"South Africa has vast tracts of land suitable for agricultural production, with 37.9% of our total land area currently being used for commercial agriculture."
South Africa's arable land is under threat from land degradation, water scarcity and urban encroachment, and is also losing prime agricultural land through land-use changes.
"Given our history, broadening access to agricultural land for commercial production and subsistence farming is a national priority," said Ramaphosa
"Although the post-1994 land reform process has resulted in more land being restored and restituted to black South Africans, the pernicious effects of the 1913 Natives Land Act continue to be in patterns of farmland ownership."
But the act went far beyond dispossessing millions of people of their ancestral land.
"By depriving our people of their right to own and work the land on which they depended for sustenance and livelihood, this great injustice effectively engineered the poverty of black South Africans," he said.
"Its aim was to destroy our people's prospects for self-reliance, independence and economic prosperity. At the most fundamental of levels, it destroyed our ability to feed ourselves."
With land ownership still concentrated in the hands of the few, and agriculture primary production and value chains mainly owned by white commercial farmers, the effects of the past remain with South Africa.
Read: How black and white farmers are coming together
"The continued monopolisation of a key means of production like land is not just an obstacle to advancing a more egalitarian society; it is also a recipe for social unrest," said Ramaphosa.
"The hunger for land to farm is growing, especially among the rural poor. And for a number of reasons, the pace of land reform in this particular sector has been slow and unsatisfactory."
In his newsletter to the nation on Monday, Ramaphosa noted that, according to the 2019 report of the Presidential Advisory Panel on Land Reform and Agriculture, "while we export food, back home, 41% of people in rural areas and 59.4% in urban areas have severely inadequate access to food."
Agrarian reform has been a priority of successive administrations since democracy.
Between 1994 and March 2018 the state has delivered 8.4 million hectares of land to previously disadvantaged individuals under the land reform programme. But this progress amounts to less than 10% of all commercial farmland.
"In my state of the nation address earlier this year I committed that state-owned agricultural land would soon be released for farming.
This is a major milestone in the agrarian reform process, and gives effect to the promise of the Freedom Charter that the land shall be shared among those who work it," said Ramaphosa.
"Our redistributive vision aims to strike a balance between social justice and redress, and enhancing agricultural output by bringing more black farmers into the mainstream of the economy."
- The government needs to ensure that land acquired for farming purposes is productively used. To safeguard the allocated state land for farming purposes, the lease is not transferable. Beneficiaries will sign a lease agreement with the state and pay a rental fee consistent with the land value;
- The state will also ensure that farmers are supported along the road to sustainability and profitability;
- As part of this programme, beneficiaries will be trained in financial management and enterprise development;
- Women, the youth and persons with disabilities will be prioritised as beneficiaries;
"The ultimate goal of releasing these land parcels is to transform the agricultural landscape by growing a new generation of farmers," said Ramaphosa.
"Leasing land under such favourable conditions must spur them to think big; to not just grow their own businesses but to advance shared wealth and prosperity in the communities in which they farm.
They must heal the deep divisions of our past. They must dispel the stereotype that only white farmers are commercially successful in South Africa, and that black farmers are perpetually ‘emerging.'
In working this land; in turning it to productive use, they will indeed turn swords into ploughshares. They will become the faces of national reconciliation."

Mali : les projets SanDi et EMU lancés pour améliorer la santé publique
La salle de conférence du ministère de la Santé et du Développement social a abrité le mercredi 15 octobre au lancement « du Projet Energie solaire et santé numérique pour le renforcement du système de santé communautaire au Mali (SanDi) et du Projet Renforcement des systèmes nationaux d’Équipes Médicales d’Urgence (EMU) ».
La cérémonie de présentation était placée sous la présidence du médecin Colonel-major Assa Badiallo Touré, ministre de la Santé et du Développement social. 
Financé par la coopération espagnole pour un montant de 990 099 Euros (648 514 845 Fcfa), « le Projet Energie solaire et santé numérique pour le renforcement du système de santé communautaire au Mali » (SanDi) vise à améliorer l’accès équitable et durable à des soins de qualité pour les populations vulnérables grâce à des solutions numériques et énergétiques. D’une durée de 18 mois, de juillet 2025 à Décembre 2026, le projet couvre les régions de Kayes, Sikasso et Bandiangara. « Le projet SanDi s’inscrit pleinement dans la mise en place en œuvre de la stratégie nationale de la santé numérique (2024-2028), de la politique nationale d’électrification rurale, et des Objectifs de Développement Durable », a souligné le ministre de la Santé et du Développement Social, le médecin Colonel-major Assa Badiallo Touré.
Quant au « Projet Renforcement des systèmes nationaux d’Équipes Médicales d’Urgence (EMU) », il est initié par le bureau région Afrique de l’Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS) et couvre quatre pays : Tchad, Cameroun, République Centrafricaine et le Mali.  Pour le cas spécifique du Mali, le projet est financé par la Direction générale de la protection civile et aux opérations d'aide humanitaire (DG ECHO) pour un montant de 1 850 000 EUR (1 211 750 000 Fcfa), dont 604 459,63 EUR (395 921 057,65 Fcfa) alloués au Mali. D’une durée de 24 mois (juin 2025 à juin 2027), l’objectif du projet est de renforcer la capacité du Mali à répondre de manière structurée, rapide et efficace aux urgences sanitaires majeures à travers l’opérationnalisation d’un système national d’Équipes Médicales d’Urgence (EMU), en cohérence avec les normes et cadres de référence internationaux. 
Plusieurs activités sont prévues dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du projet « EMU ». Selon le représentant du Bureau de l’OMS au Mali, Dr Itama Mayikuli Christian, elles comprennent : la Mise en place d’un effectif de 80 professionnels de santé formés et préparés à être mobilisés dans les 72 heures en cas d’urgence ; Développement de procédures opérationnelles standardisées (SOPs) pour l’activation, la mobilisation et le déploiement des EMU ; Réalisation d’exercices de simulation pour tester l’état de préparation face aux épidémies et aux urgences de santé publique.
Il convient de rappeler que la cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence de l’Ambassadeur du Royaume d’Espagne au Mali ainsi que de la Chargée d’Affaires de la Délégation de l’Union Européenne au Mali Bettina Muscheidt.
Abdrahamane SISSOKO/maliweb.net
a1571.en:
Mali: SanDi and EMU projects launched to improve public health

The conference room of the Ministry of Health and Social Development hosted, on Wednesday 15 October, the launch of "the Solar Energy and Digital Health Project for strengthening the community health system in Mali (SanDi) and the Project for Strengthening National Emergency Medical Teams (EMU) Systems."

The presentation ceremony was chaired by Colonel-Major (physician) Assa Badiallo Touré, Minister of Health and Social Development.

Funded by Spanish cooperation in the amount of 990,099 euros (648,514,845 CFA francs), "the Solar Energy and Digital Health Project for strengthening the community health system in Mali" (SanDi) aims to improve equitable and sustainable access to quality care for vulnerable populations through digital and energy solutions. Lasting 18 months, from July 2025 to December 2026, the project covers the regions of Kayes, Sikasso and Bandiagara. "The SanDi project fits fully within the implementation of the national digital health strategy (2024-2028), the national rural electrification policy, and the Sustainable Development Goals," stressed the Minister of Health and Social Development, Colonel-Major (physician) Assa Badiallo Touré.

As for the "Project for Strengthening National Emergency Medical Teams (EMU) Systems," it was initiated by the Africa Regional Office of the World Health Organization (WHO) and covers four countries: Chad, Cameroon, the Central African Republic and Mali. In Mali's specific case, the project is funded by the Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (DG ECHO) in the amount of 1,850,000 EUR (1,211,750,000 CFA francs), of which 604,459.63 EUR (395,921,057.65 CFA francs) is allocated to Mali. Lasting 24 months (June 2025 to June 2027), the project's objective is to strengthen Mali's capacity to respond in a structured, rapid and effective manner to major health emergencies through the operationalization of a national Emergency Medical Teams (EMU) system, in line with international standards and reference frameworks.

Several activities are planned as part of the implementation of the "EMU" project. According to the representative of the WHO Office in Mali, Dr. Itama Mayikuli Christian, they include: the establishment of a cohort of 80 health professionals trained and prepared to be mobilized within 72 hours in the event of an emergency; the development of standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the activation, mobilization and deployment of the EMUs; and the conduct of simulation exercises to test preparedness for epidemics and public health emergencies.

It should be recalled that the ceremony took place in the presence of the Ambassador of the Kingdom of Spain to Mali as well as the Chargée d'Affaires of the Delegation of the European Union to Mali, Bettina Muscheidt.

Abdrahamane SISSOKO/maliweb.net

a1721.t:
Dr Sié Kambou est spécialiste en biologie et écologie végétales. Après un séjour au Danemark et en Suisse dans le cadre des recherches, il est, de nos jours, responsable de la division de recherche appliquée au Centre national de semence forestière (CNSF). Sidwaya s’est entretenu avec lui sur la question des biotechnologies et de leur apport dans la protection de l’environnement.
Sidwaya (S) : Qu’est-ce que la biotechnologie ou la modification génétique des produits ?
Sié Kambou (S.K.) : Il n’y a pas une seule définition typique de la biotechnologie. Lorsqu’on fermente le dolo, c’est de la biotechnologie, parce qu’on utilise des organismes vivants pour produire l’alcool. De même, quand on fait la fermentation du soumbala, c’est aussi de la biotechnologie. La biotechnologie implique fortement les organismes vivants ; on va obliger ces derniers à produire ce dont nous avons besoin. On peut donc dire que la biotechnologie ou la modification génétique des produits est l’utilisation des propriétés des orga-nismes pour la production des matières et services au bénéfice de l’humanité.
S : Quel lien peut-on faire entre le greffage et le clonage ?
S.K. : Le greffage consiste à implanter dans les tissus d’un fragment quelconque prélevé sur une autre plante ou de la même plante pour que celui-ci continue à croître, en faisant corps avec la première. Et comme le greffage répond à la question de comment pouvoir produire une variété donnée identique en plusieurs, nous dirons que le greffage est aussi du clonage, puisque c’est des copies identiques à l’arbre désiré qu’on a produites.
S : Que comprendre par culture génétiquement modifiée (OGM) ?
S.K. : Il faut savoir que le génétiquement modifié existe dans la nature. En réalité, il existe dans la nature une bactérie appelée Basileus turgescent (Bt) qui infecte des plantes et leur injecte certains gènes pour les obliger à lui produire des protéines avec lesquelles elle se nourrit. Dans la nature, les choses sont déterminées par des gènes. La couleur des yeux, de la peau, la taille… sont le fait des gènes. Et c’est cette logique que les chercheurs suivent dans leur travail. Ce n’est pas une invention de l’esprit. Partant de ce constat, on se dit que forcer la plante à produire ce dont on a besoin n’est pas mauvais. Par exemple, dans le domaine de la médecine on oblige certains organismes à produire la pénicilline pour l’homme. Dans le cadre des OGM, on peut schématiser suivant l’exemple de la murette. On veut clôturer un espace avec une murette de deux couches complétée avec du grillage. On construit le mur en deux couches avec des briques en parping. Il se trouve que dans votre construction, il y a des passages d’eau que vous n’avez pas prévus et lors de la saison hivernale, une partie du mur est emportée par l’eau de ruissellement. Vous décidez de la réparer en utilisant des briques en pierres. A la fin, vous aurez un mur dont une partie est en pierres et l’autre en parping, et vous mettez de la tyrolienne.
S : Est- ce qu’il y a un problème ?
S.K. : Il n’y a pas de problème et vous avez votre mur. C’est cela les OGM, la culture des produits génétiquement modifiés.
S : Que reproche-t-on au coton Bt ?
S.K.: Je préfère vous référer à l’INERA qui a beaucoup travaillé là-dessus. Cependant, il faut noter que le coton Bt utilise moins de pesticides et cela est économiquement rentable pour nos cotonculteurs. La différence entre le coton Bt et le coton local réside dans la longueur des fibres. Il faut, pour ce faire, effectuer plusieurs traitements pour le coton Bt et c’est cela que les industriels déplorent, car cela leur coûte cher. En tant que chercheur, on pouvait donc continuer les recherches pour comprendre pourquoi ces fibres sont-elles moins longues et ainsi de suite jusqu’à obtenir ce qu’on veut.
S : Pourquoi les populations sont frileuses face aux produits GM ?
S.K. : Les Etats-Unis sont les premiers à travailler sur les OGM, et l’opinion publique n’en fait pas un problème. Le soja, le maïs sont cultivés sur des milliers d’hectares et cela ne pose pas de problème chez les Américains. Le problème, c’est au niveau des Européens, mais cela ne les empêche pas de conti-nuer à travailler sur les OGM, car ils savent que le génétiquement modifié existe dans la nature à travers le Basileus turgescente (Bt). La communication sur le rejet de la consommation des produits OGM est le fait des agitateurs. Sinon, comment comprendre que l’on veuille renier ce qui existe dans la nature ? De nos jours, plus de 60% de soja est produit à partir du soja OGM ; on n’en fait pas un problème et il est consommé partout. Je dis donc qu’il est bon qu’il y ait des gens qui soient «contre» pour que ceux qui sont «pour» prennent les précautions pour respecter l’éthique.
S : En quoi la biotechnologie peut-elle participer à la protection de l’environnement ?
S.K. : Les OGM peuvent nous permettre d’avoir des plantes qui résistent aux pesticides, et nous libérer de leur utilisation. Cela n’est-il pas mieux que d’arroser l’environnement avec des herbicides et autres? Et c’est là l’importance des OGM pour la protection de l’environnement. La quantité des pesticides qui entrent au Burkina Faso chaque année, constituent un danger public parce que vous rompez une chaîne alimentaire. Les herbicides détruisent les plantes dont se nourrissent les insectes ; les insectes qui mangent ces plantes meurent ; les oiseaux qui mangent ces insectes vont aussi mourir de même que les autres animaux qui vont manger ces oiseaux et par la suite, l’homme du village va se saisir de cet animal mort et le consommer à son tour. Si on pèse les pour et les contre, en expliquant bien ce que sont les OGM et ce qu’est l’apport des pesticides, je crois que la population va préférer consommer OGM.
S : La peur des risques peut-elle justifier le rejet des avantages des cultures génétiquement modifiées ?
S.K. : Le rejet des cultures génétiquement modifiées ne peut s’expliquer que pour deux raisons que sont l’éthique et la dépendance des grandes firmes ou sociétés pour l’obtention des sources d’approvisionnement des semences. L’éthique dont les gens parlent, c’est d’enlever un gène animal et l’introduire dans la plante ou prendre un gène chez l’homme et l’introduire dans la plante. Sinon l’OGM permet de s’affranchir des barrières naturelles. Par exemple, vous ne pouvez pas croiser un manguier avec un citronnier, mais vous pouvez prélever un gène de résistance chez le manguier si cela est intéressant et l’introduire chez le citronnier parce que naturellement cela ne peut pas se faire. Les hommes, par précaution, ont peur de ce qui est nouveau, exemple de Louis Pasteur à la découverte du sérum antirabique. Mais quand on a vu le succès du sérum, il s’est répandu et on l’utilise encore de nos jours. C’est normal qu’on ait un peu peur de ce dont on n’a pas l’habitude, mais cela ne justifie pas qu’on arrête les travaux là-dessus. Et on ne peut pas arrêter le progrès. Qu’on le veuille ou pas, on ne peut pas arrêter aujourd’hui de produire OGM ; cela va même s’amplifier, car les OGM nous rendent d’énormes services. Maintenant c’est bon que le chercheur prenne des précautions et que les pays pauvres se mettent à la page de la technologie. Nous avons des hommes capables de travailler sur les OGM, il suffit de les équiper. Et la preuve, quand MONSANTO est venu, il a travaillé avec des Burkinabè. Ils ont bien travaillé, car ils sont très bien formés.
S : Mais MONSANTO est décrié…
S.K. : Monsanto n’a pas trop de problèmes avec les OGM ; il a beaucoup plus de problème avec l’herbicide tel que le gluconate. Monsanto ne travaille pas seulement sur les OGM. Je n’ai pas encore vu un article qui met en cause l’utilisation des OGM qui soient nuisibles à l’homme. Il n’y a pas un écrit scientifique qui le prouve.
S : Quelle posture souhaitez-vous pour le Burkina face aux OGM ?
S.K. : L’avantage qu’on a au Burkina est indéniable. Nous sommes l’un des rares pays en Afrique à avoir une agence nationale de biosécurité qui permet de contrôler tout ce qui est lié aux organismes modifiés. En tant que Burkinabè, humain, le chercheur n’est pas prêt à mettre à la disposition des autres un produit qui n’est pas bien. Le chercheur a un devoir moral de ne pas mettre à la disposition de la population des produits dont la consommation est nuisible à leur santé. La consommation bio est une question de mode qui ne veut pas dire forcément anti OGM, mais plutôt anti pesticide et les produits OGM sont aussi sur cette lancée. Pour moi, on ne peut pas arrêter le progrès ; on a plutôt intérêt à accompagner le progrès et à disposer des équipements et des laboratoires qui puissent être à la pointe de cette nouvelle technologie qui si elle est utilisée à bon escient est très utile pour nous-mêmes.
ADEGUEROU Waliou A.
a1721.en:
Dr Sié Kambou is a specialist in plant biology and ecology. After a stay in Denmark and Switzerland as part of his research, he is today head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF). Sidwaya spoke with him about biotechnology and its contribution to environmental protection.

Sidwaya (S): What is biotechnology or the genetic modification of products?

Sié Kambou (S.K.): There is no single typical definition of biotechnology. When you ferment dolo, that is biotechnology, because living organisms are used to produce alcohol. Likewise, when soumbala is fermented, that too is biotechnology. Biotechnology strongly involves living organisms; we oblige them to produce what we need. We can therefore say that biotechnology, or the genetic modification of products, is the use of the properties of organisms to produce goods and services for the benefit of humanity.

S: What connection can be made between grafting and cloning?

S.K.: Grafting consists of implanting into the tissues a fragment taken from another plant or from the same plant so that it continues to grow, becoming one with the first. And since grafting answers the question of how to produce several identical copies of a given variety, we would say that grafting is also cloning, since what is produced are identical copies of the desired tree.

S: What should we understand by genetically modified crops (GMOs)?

S.K.: You have to know that the genetically modified exists in nature. In reality, there exists in nature a bacterium called Basileus turgescent (Bt) which infects plants and injects certain genes into them to force them to produce proteins that it feeds on. In nature, things are determined by genes. Eye colour, skin colour, height... are the work of genes. And it is this logic that researchers follow in their work. It is not an invention of the mind. Starting from that observation, one concludes that forcing the plant to produce what we need is not a bad thing. For example, in the field of medicine we force certain organisms to produce penicillin for man. In the case of GMOs, it can be illustrated with the example of a low wall. You want to enclose a space with a two-layer low wall topped with wire mesh. You build the wall in two layers with breeze blocks. It turns out that in your construction there are water channels you had not anticipated, and during the rainy season part of the wall is carried away by run-off water. You decide to repair it using stone blocks. In the end you will have a wall of which one part is stone and the other breeze block, and you apply roughcast render.

S: Is there a problem?

S.K.: There is no problem and you have your wall. That is what GMOs are, the cultivation of genetically modified products.

S: What is held against Bt cotton?

S.K.: I would rather refer you to INERA, which has worked a great deal on this. However, it should be noted that Bt cotton uses fewer pesticides and that is economically profitable for our cotton growers. The difference between Bt cotton and local cotton lies in the length of the fibres. Several treatments have to be carried out for Bt cotton, and that is what the industrial processors deplore, because it costs them dearly. As a researcher, one could therefore continue the research to understand why these fibres are shorter, and so on until we obtain what we want.

S: Why are people wary of GM products?

S.K.: The United States was the first to work on GMOs, and public opinion does not make an issue of it. Soya and maize are grown over thousands of hectares and that poses no problem for Americans. The problem is at the level of the Europeans, but that does not stop them from continuing to work on GMOs, because they know that the genetically modified exists in nature through Basileus turgescente (Bt). The messaging about rejecting the consumption of GMO products is the work of agitators. Otherwise, how can one understand wanting to deny what exists in nature? Nowadays, more than 60% of soya is produced from GMO soya; no one makes an issue of it and it is consumed everywhere. I therefore say it is good that there are people who are "against" so that those who are "for" take precautions to respect ethics.

S: How can biotechnology contribute to protecting the environment?

S.K.: GMOs can allow us to have plants that resist pesticides, and free us from their use. Is that not better than drenching the environment with herbicides and the like? And that is the importance of GMOs for protecting the environment. The quantity of pesticides that enter Burkina Faso each year constitutes a public danger because you break a food chain. Herbicides destroy the plants that insects feed on; the insects that eat these plants die; the birds that eat these insects will also die, as will the other animals that eat those birds, and afterwards the villager will pick up that dead animal and consume it in turn. If we weigh the pros and cons, explaining clearly what GMOs are and what pesticides contribute, I believe the population will prefer to consume GMOs.

S: Can fear of the risks justify rejecting the advantages of genetically modified crops?

S.K.: The rejection of genetically modified crops can only be explained by two reasons: ethics, and dependence on large firms or companies for obtaining sources of seed supply. The ethics people speak of is taking an animal gene and introducing it into a plant, or taking a gene from a human and introducing it into a plant. Otherwise GMOs make it possible to overcome natural barriers. For example, you cannot cross a mango tree with a lemon tree, but you can take a resistance gene from the mango tree, if that is of interest, and introduce it into the lemon tree, because naturally that cannot happen. Human beings, out of caution, are afraid of what is new, like Louis Pasteur at the discovery of the rabies serum. But when the success of the serum was seen, it spread and it is still used today. It is normal to be a little afraid of what one is not used to, but that does not justify stopping work on it. And progress cannot be stopped. Whether we like it or not, we cannot stop producing GMOs today; it will even expand, because GMOs render us enormous services. Now it is good that the researcher takes precautions and that poor countries get up to date with the technology. We have men capable of working on GMOs, they simply need to be equipped. And the proof: when MONSANTO came, it worked with Burkinabè. They worked well, because they are very well trained.

S: But MONSANTO is criticised...

S.K.: Monsanto does not have too many problems with GMOs; it has far more problems with herbicides such as gluconate. Monsanto does not work only on GMOs. I have not yet seen an article implicating the use of GMOs as harmful to man. There is no scientific writing that proves it.

S: What stance do you wish Burkina to take on GMOs?

S.K.: The advantage we have in Burkina is undeniable. We are one of the few countries in Africa to have a national biosafety agency that makes it possible to control everything connected with modified organisms. As a Burkinabè, as a human being, the researcher is not prepared to make available to others a product that is not good. The researcher has a moral duty not to make available to the population products whose consumption is harmful to their health. Organic consumption is a matter of fashion which does not necessarily mean anti-GMO, but rather anti-pesticide, and GMO products are also on that same trajectory. For me, progress cannot be stopped; we have more to gain from supporting progress and from having equipment and laboratories that can be at the cutting edge of this new technology which, if used wisely, is very useful for ourselves.

ADEGUEROU Waliou A.

a1779.t:
L’éradication de la soif et la facilité d’accès à l’eau potable et l’assainissement constituent l’une des priorités absolues du gouvernement, notamment le MAEPE-RH. Faire de ce vœu une réalité concrète et mettre les populations des zones rurales à l’abri des difficultés liées au stress hydrique sont les nobles missions que poursuit sans relâche la direction de l’hydraulique rurale du ministère de l’agriculture de l’élevage, de la pêche et des ressources halieutiques jusqu’aux recoins les plus reculés de notre territoire national. L’absence d’outils valorisant ces données accentue les difficultés du secteur.
En effet, la réalisation d’une plateforme d’information sur l’eau et l’assainissement est plus qu’indispensable. C’est dans ce cadre précis que le MAEPE-RH, à travers la DHR, a pris l’initiative de mettre en place le protocole national du système de suivi et d’évaluation pour le secteur WASH en milieu rural avec l’appui financier de l’USAID par le biais de l’UNICEF. La consultation a démarré au mois de septembre 2018 avec le cabinet ‘‘Cosinus’’, retenu pour la mise en place de cet outil. Lors de la phase élaboration du document, la DHR a associé l’ensemble des acteurs du secteur. D’ailleurs, les informations collectées dans ce cadre ont servi de référence dans la formulation des principaux axes du protocole. Lequel a fait l’objet de partage par email à toutes les parties prenantes afin de servir de base aux discussions de l’atelier. De façon spécifique, les objectifs poursuivis par le protocole sont de définir le cadre de mesure de la performance des indicateurs du secteur en milieu rural, d’élaborer de façon consensuelle les procédures de collecte, de traitement, d’analyse et de diffusion des données afin de renseigner sur l’efficacité et l’efficience du secteur, en comparant les résultats obtenus avec le niveau de mobilisation des ressources humaines et financières, de déterminer le rôle que chaque structure intervenant dans le secteur en milieu rural doit jouer dans l’animation du protocole, d’assurer le fonctionnement d’un système de gestion de l’information inclusif et intégré qui garantit une accessibilité aux données de performance en temps réel, gage d’une prise de décision soutenue par des éléments probants. Il est indispensable pour nous que le secteur du WASH ait un regard qualitatif sur ce document en vue de partager leur expertise durant les trois jours de l’atelier.
a1779.en:
"The creation of an information platform on water and sanitation is more than indispensable" — Ibrahim Elmi Mohamed, Secretary General of the MAEPE-R

The eradication of thirst and easy access to drinking water and sanitation constitute one of the government's absolute priorities, notably for the MAEPE-RH. Making this wish a concrete reality and sheltering the populations of rural areas from the difficulties linked to water stress are the noble missions relentlessly pursued by the Rural Hydraulics Directorate of the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Fisheries Resources, reaching into the most remote corners of our national territory. The absence of tools that make use of these data accentuates the sector's difficulties.

Indeed, the creation of an information platform on water and sanitation is more than indispensable. It is within this precise framework that the MAEPE-RH, through the DHR, took the initiative of establishing the national protocol for the monitoring and evaluation system for the WASH sector in rural areas, with the financial support of USAID through UNICEF. The consultancy began in September 2018 with the firm "Cosinus", selected to put this tool in place. During the drafting phase of the document, the DHR involved all of the sector's stakeholders. Indeed, the information collected in this framework served as a reference in the formulation of the protocol's main pillars. The protocol was shared by email with all the stakeholders so that it could serve as a basis for the workshop's discussions. Specifically, the objectives pursued by the protocol are: to define the framework for measuring the performance of the sector's indicators in rural areas; to draw up in a consensual manner the procedures for collecting, processing, analysing and disseminating data in order to provide information on the sector's effectiveness and efficiency, by comparing the results obtained with the level of mobilisation of human and financial resources; to determine the role that each structure involved in the sector in rural areas must play in running the protocol; and to ensure the functioning of an inclusive and integrated information management system that guarantees accessibility to performance data in real time, a guarantee of decision-making supported by conclusive evidence. It is indispensable for us that the WASH sector take a qualitative look at this document in order to share their expertise during the three days of the workshop.

a1832.t:
The Export Development Fund (EDF) more than doubled its support for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in 2024, disbursing K14.1 billion up from K6 billion in 2023 with a focus on agro-processing, tourism and mining.
Agro-processing alone accounted for 56 percent of total disbursements, followed by tourism at 30 percent and mining at eight percent.
EDF’s 2024 Integrated Annual Report shows the fund’s net profit rose to K18.9 billion from K9.7 billion the previous year while its total assets grew to K115.7 billion from K95.1 billion in 2023.
The gains came despite high inflation, foreign exchange shortages and gross domestic product growth slowing to 1.8 percent in 2024.
EDF said its investment strategy aligns with national priorities under Malawi 2063, focusing on sectors with clear economic and social value.
In 2024, EDF-financed projects created or preserved 791 jobs, 420 of them benefiting women and youth, bringing the total employment impact to over 40 000 jobs since its inception.
Yet despite these advances, concerns persist over transparency and equitable access. Economist Velli Nyirongo said in an interview that EDF plays a catalytic role in easing financing constraints, but its impact on SME-led industrialisation and export diversification remains limited in scope.
“Many beneficiaries are concentrated in urban centres, while rural-based and informal SMEs, particularly women- and youth-led enterprises—remain underserved,” he said.
Mach Milk Company factory manager Hastings Thondolo said in an interview on Friday that limited access to capital hinders his firm’s ability to fulfil large-scale contracts.
“At the moment, we are supplying some local shops in Blantyre, but we do not have the finances required to finance a long-term contract demanded by major retail chains such as Chipiku and Shoprite,” he said.
Thondolo said the absence of publicly available impact data, makes it difficult to assess how EDF financing translates into exports or industrial transformation.
EDF continues to pursue strategic initiatives as in 2024, its Precious Metals and Minerals Unit purchased 131 kilogrammes (kg) of gold, exceeding its 100kg target, bringing the cumulative total to 302kg valued at $25.7 million (about K45 billion).
The unit seeks to stabilise gold prices, support small-scale miners and promote responsible trade.
EDF also expanded gemstone exports to markets in Germany, Sri Lanka and the United States.
On the agribusiness front, EDF enabled Nascomex, the commercial arm of National Association of Smallholders in Malawi (Nasfam) to supply maize grits to Castel Malawi, reducing import reliance.
EDF also financed the construction of Rudevit’s organic fertiliser plant in Blantyre, expected to create at least 100 jobs and reduce fertiliser import dependency.
In the cannabis sector, EDF supported MMC Limited to establish a medicinal cannabis processing facility in Lilongwe, projected to generate up to $100 million (about K175 billion) annually in export revenue and employ over 50 people.
The investment, made through a mix of debt and equity, signals a shift away from reliance on tobacco towards high-value, legal exports.

Dans le cadre des relations historiques et séculaires existant entre la République de Djibouti et la République Arabe d’Egypte, S.E.M. Abdulfatah Al-Sissi a effectué une visite à Djibouti ce jeudi 27 Mai 2021. Fidèle à son hospitalité traditionnelle et désirant témoigner de l’excellence des relations fraternelles des deux peuples, Djibouti a réservé au Président Egyptien un accueil particulièrement chaleureux. Au cours de la visite, les Deux Chefs d’Etat ont eu un tête à tête ainsi qu’une réunion de consultation élargie au Palais présidentiel à laquelle ont pris part les Hauts Responsables égyptiens et Djiboutiens. Les discussions qui se sont déroulées dans une atmosphère empreinte de fraternité et de compréhension mutuelle ont permis d’examiner les voies et moyens de renforcer les relations bilatérales et la coopération. Les deux parties ont échangé leurs points de vue sur les questions régionales, arabes et internationales d’intérêt commun et ont constaté la convergence de leurs opinions sur les différents points abordés.
Les Deux Dirigeants ont salué leur volonté commune de resserrer davantage leur relation stratégique et se sont engagés à déployer plus d’efforts pour développer la coopération bilatérale en redynamisant les mécanismes du travail commun, notamment dans le cadre de la 4ème commission mixte ministérielle qui s’est tenue au Caire en Janvier 2010 ainsi que la concertation politique.
Lls ont également souligné la nécessiter d’explorer de nouveaux horizons pour hisser nos relations fraternelles au plus haut niveau dans tous les domaines, tels que le renforcement des échanges commerciaux, la coopération économique, la création de la zone logistique égyptienne, la coopération interportuaire, l’éducation, l’enseignement supérieur, la santé notamment à travers le projet de création d’un hôpital égyptien à Djibouti en collaboration avec le ministère de la santé, le renforcement des capacités, la pêche et les ressources halieutiques, l’énergie, le pétrole, le gaz naturel, l’habitat, la construction des routes, le tourisme, les banques ainsi que la lutte contre le terrorisme et l‘extrémisme.
Le Président de la République a exprimé son appréciation quant aux réalisations enregistrées et efforts consentis, sous la vision éclairée du Président Al-Sissi, pour promouvoir le développement économique et assurer la sécurité et de la stabilité de l’Egypte.
Les deux Chefs d’Etats ont échangé sur les mesures prises ainsi que les efforts déployés pour lutter contre la pandémie du coronavirus et les conséquences sanitaires, sociales et économiques que cette crise a provoquées. A cet effet, le gouvernement djiboutien a exprimé ses vifs remerciements pour le don d’équipements, de matériel médical, de denrées alimentaires et les équipements pour personnes à besoins spéciaux que le gouvernement égyptien a, dans un élan de solidarité fraternelle, offert au peuple djiboutien pour faire face à cette pandémie.
Les deux parties ont réaffirmé l’importance d’instaurer une meilleure concertation entre les pays riverains de la Mer Rouge, pour renforcer la sécurité et la stabilité de la région, une voie stratégique du trafic maritime et du commerce international et ce, par le biais de mécanismes communs.
Les discussions ont également porté sur la question du barrage de la renaissance et les deux parties ont convenu que le Nil doit constituer un moyen de coopération permettant de réaliser les objectifs de développement de l’Egypte, du Soudan et de l’Ethiopie. Les deux parties ont réaffirmé la nécessité de reprendre les négociations afin de parvenir à un accord pouvant préserver les intérêts des trois pays, empêcher tout dommage et accompagner les efforts de prospérité et de stabilité dans toute la région.
Concernant la question palestinienne, le Président de la République a salué le succès de l’initiative égyptienne du cessez le feu qui a permis de mettre fin à l’agression israélienne et de sauver la vie à nos frères palestiniens.
Les deux parties ont souligné la nécessité de poursuivre les efforts pour parvenir à une issue globale et permanente basée sur la solution de deux états permettant à la Palestine de revenir aux frontières de Juin 1967 avec Jérusalem Est comme Capitale, conformément à l’initiative arabe et aux résolutions internationales.
Le Président de la République Arabe d’Egypte, S.E.M. Abdulfatah AI-Sissi a tenu à remercier Son Homologue Djiboutien, S.E Ismail Omar Guelleh pour l’accueil chaleureux et la généreuse hospitalité dont sa délégation et lui-même ont fait l’objet et l’a, à son tour, invité à effectuer une visite en Egypte.
Communiqué du ministère des affaires étrangères et de la coopération internationale
a1887.en:
Within the framework of the historic and centuries-old relations existing between the Republic of Djibouti and the Arab Republic of Egypt, H.E. Mr Abdulfatah Al-Sissi made a visit to Djibouti on Thursday 27 May 2021. Faithful to its traditional hospitality and wishing to demonstrate the excellence of the fraternal relations between the two peoples, Djibouti gave the Egyptian President a particularly warm welcome. During the visit, the two Heads of State held a one-on-one meeting as well as an expanded consultation meeting at the presidential palace, in which senior Egyptian and Djiboutian officials took part. The discussions, which took place in an atmosphere marked by fraternity and mutual understanding, made it possible to examine ways and means of strengthening bilateral relations and cooperation. The two sides exchanged their points of view on regional, Arab and international questions of common interest and noted the convergence of their opinions on the various points addressed.
The two Leaders welcomed their common desire to further tighten their strategic relationship and committed to deploying more efforts to develop bilateral cooperation by revitalising the mechanisms of joint work, notably within the framework of the 4th joint ministerial commission held in Cairo in January 2010, as well as political consultation.
They also underlined the need to explore new horizons in order to raise our fraternal relations to the highest level in all fields, such as strengthening trade exchanges, economic cooperation, the creation of the Egyptian logistics zone, inter-port cooperation, education, higher education, health — notably through the project to create an Egyptian hospital in Djibouti in collaboration with the ministry of health — capacity building, fishing and fishery resources, energy, petroleum, natural gas, housing, road construction, tourism, banking, as well as the fight against terrorism and extremism.
The President of the Republic expressed his appreciation for the achievements recorded and the efforts made, under the enlightened vision of President Al-Sissi, to promote economic development and ensure the security and stability of Egypt.
The two Heads of State exchanged views on the measures taken as well as the efforts deployed to fight the coronavirus pandemic and the health, social and economic consequences this crisis has caused. To this effect, the Djiboutian government expressed its keen thanks for the donation of equipment, medical supplies, foodstuffs and equipment for people with special needs that the Egyptian government, in a surge of fraternal solidarity, offered to the Djiboutian people to confront this pandemic.
The two parties reaffirmed the importance of establishing better consultation between the countries bordering the Red Sea, in order to strengthen the security and stability of the region, a strategic route for maritime traffic and international trade, through joint mechanisms.
The discussions also covered the question of the Renaissance Dam and the two parties agreed that the Nile must constitute a means of cooperation allowing the development objectives of Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia to be achieved. The two parties reaffirmed the necessity of resuming negotiations in order to reach an agreement that can preserve the interests of the three countries, prevent any damage and accompany efforts for prosperity and stability throughout the region.
Concerning the Palestinian question, the President of the Republic welcomed the success of the Egyptian ceasefire initiative which made it possible to put an end to the Israeli aggression and save the lives of our Palestinian brothers.
The two parties underlined the need to pursue efforts to reach a comprehensive and permanent outcome based on the two-state solution allowing Palestine to return to the June 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its Capital, in accordance with the Arab initiative and international resolutions.
The President of the Arab Republic of Egypt, H.E. Mr Abdulfatah Al-Sissi, wished to thank his Djiboutian Counterpart, H.E. Ismail Omar Guelleh, for the warm welcome and the generous hospitality which his delegation and he himself received, and in turn invited him to make a visit to Egypt.
Communiqué of the ministry of foreign affairs and international cooperation

It is the first week of school for three of the Haingura sisters, and though they’re understandably apprehensive about their new environment, there’s a sense of renewed hope in the air.
Once dimmed by hardship, their dreams for the future are rekindled thanks to the support from the USAID/President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR)-funded Reach Namibia programme.
The Haingura family, four siblings from the Tondoro constituency in Kavango West, were left to fend for themselves after both their parents left the village in search of better economic opportunities. Initially, financial support trickled in, but it soon dwindled, leaving 14-year-old Kalista, the second-eldest, with the overwhelming responsibility of caring for her siblings.
Despite these challenges, the sisters showed remarkable resilience. Reach Namibia, a programme launched in 2023 to prevent new HIV infections and improve treatment outcomes for HIV-positive children and adolescents, first learned of the Haingura siblings’ plight in April 2024. A life skills teacher at their former school brought the case to the attention of a community care worker in Kavango West, demonstrating the power of community in supporting those in need.
“I couldn’t bear to see the conditions these children were living in. Their field had not produced crops in years, leaving them nothing to eat. It broke my heart as a mother, so I opened my home to them,” recalls Sofia Murangi.
The educator went beyond providing shelter, offering the children a safe place to sleep at night. She was particularly concerned about the dangers they faced from some local men, who had been reported to make advances towards the minors. The challenges faced by child-headed households extend far beyond the daily struggle for survival.
“Without the guidance and support of parents, these young heads of families often struggle to meet basic needs like food, education and healthcare,” stated Klara Kakororo, Reach Namibia’s Orphans and Vulnerable Children technical director.
“The emotional burden of losing their childhood to these responsibilities leaves them isolated, stressed and vulnerable to exploitation. This cycle not only jeopardizes their future, but also has a ripple-effect on the wider community, threatening the long-term social and economic stability of the region,” she added.
Support for the family has led to positive change. With the help of the programme and the Ministry of Gender Equality, Poverty Eradication and Social Welfare, 17-year-old Milka, who has a hearing impairment, has had her social grant reinstated, which helps with her upkeep in Rundu.
The line ministry has played a crucial role in ensuring the family receives the necessary support and resources for their well-being. Meanwhile, Kalista (14), Theresia (12), and Mariane (9) are slowly acclimatising to their new setting at Simanya Combined School.
With the help of a social worker, the girls have also been enrolled in the school’s hostel, with Sofia Murangi stepping in as their primary caregiver during the holidays. Furthermore, the trio benefits from the supply of uniforms, stationery, and toiletries (among other essentials).
Mariane’s class teacher has already noticed the 9-year-old’s cheerful spirit. “In the first week of school, she has made friends, and her classmates have been very welcoming.
However, we’re also mindful of the circumstances that brought the girls here, so we ensure that the life skills teacher continuously assesses their academic and psycho-social development.”
They were inspired by the support she’s received from social worker Ndinelao Joseph and Kalista dreams of pursuing a career in human sciences.
Her aspirations, filled with hope and determination, are a testament to the positive impact of the support she and her siblings have received.

a2207.t:
President John Dramani Mahama has outlined plans to reshape Ghana’s economy through a 24-hour economy policy and a $10 billion infrastructure project, aimed at boosting job creation, industrial growth, and reducing reliance on foreign aid.
Speaking at Ghana’s Independence Day celebration on March 6, 2025, Mr Mahama stressed the need for a shift in the country’s economic approach, arguing that round-the-clock productivity is key to reversing years of stagnation.
“The era of an economy that sleeps at night must end. Ghana needs continuous productivity, more jobs, and a stronger export base. The 24-hour economy is not just a policy, it is a necessity,” he said.
He explained that under this initiative, businesses will be encouraged to operate throughout the day and night, and the government will work to provide stable electricity, improved security, and better transport systems to support night-time production and trade.
Beyond the 24-hour economy, Mr Mahama also spoke about his $10 billion ‘Big Push’ infrastructure plan, which he said would expand roads, railways, and energy systems while creating thousands of jobs.
“This is a bold step towards building a Ghana that stands on its own industries and workforce instead of continuously seeking foreign assistance,” he said.
Mr Mahama also stressed the role of agriculture in reducing import dependence, pointing to his administration’s Agriculture for Economic Transformation Agenda, which seeks to strengthen local food production and cut Ghana’s $2 billion annual food import bill.
He said initiatives such as the Feed Ghana Programme and the Farm-to-Table Poultry Initiative would give farmers access to land, mechanised farming tools, and inputs while promoting large-scale food processing to help stabilise prices.
“Our future prosperity depends on our ability to feed ourselves, produce what we consume, and export more than we import. That is the foundation of true economic independence,” he said.
Mr Mahama urged Ghanaians to support policies aimed at reducing dependence on donor aid, IMF bailouts, and excessive imports, insisting that the path to economic stability lies in productivity, innovation, and disciplined governance.
